title: Give a Warning That Means Something | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: Five minutes left can become four more warnings until nobody believes the clock. Repeating a direction without acting teaches a child to wait for the louder or later version. Before the warning, choose the exact final activity and what will happen next. Say: Two more turns on the slide, then we hold hands to the path; count the turns calmly and follow through after the second. The purpose of a warning is predictability, not bargaining; use one clear cue, an observable ending, and steady action.

source.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source.title: Tips for Giving Directions
